title: Following instructions
examples: Can you show me what it means to listen carefully?
What is the difference between one instruction and two instructions?
What should I do if I forget what you just said?

explain.say: Listen to me say this sentence. I will say, 'Touch your nose.'
You just heard one simple thing to do. That is following one instruction.
Now listen carefully to this. I will say, 'Clap your hands and then stomp your feet.'
You did two things in order. That is following two instructions.

faq.q: What if I only do the first thing you say?
faq.a: You only did the first part of the instructions. Remember to listen for everything I say.
asks: What if I stop after the first action?
Do I have to do everything you say?

faq.q: Is listening the same as hearing?
faq.a: Hearing is when sound comes to your ears. Listening means you pay attention to the words.
asks: What is the difference between hearing and listening?
Do I just need to hear you talk?

faq.q: Do I have to do the steps in order?
faq.a: Yes, the order is very important. You must do the first thing before you do the second thing.
asks: Can I do the second thing first?
Does the order matter when I follow directions?

faq.q: What should I do if I get confused?
faq.a: It is okay to feel confused. You can look at me or ask me to say it again slowly.
asks: What if I forget what you said?
Can you repeat the instructions if I get mixed up?

faq.q: Are two steps always harder than one step?
faq.a: Sometimes two steps are a little harder, but it helps your brain get stronger. You can try your best!
asks: Is two steps always more work?
Will I get better at following steps?

facts: Listening means paying attention to what someone says.
One-step instructions ask you to do only one thing.
Two-step instructions ask you to do two things in order.
When we listen, we use our ears and our brains.

quiz.say: If I say, 'Point to your head.' What is the action?
quiz.show: One step: Point to your head.
quiz.why: This is only one thing you need to do, so it is one step.

wrong.0: This is a different action and not what I asked you to do.
wrong.1: This is two actions, but I only asked for one action.
wrong.2: This is an action, but it is not the specific action I gave you.

quiz.say: If I say, 'Jump up and then sit down.' What is the order?

options.show: Jump up first, then sit down.
options.say: Jump up first, then sit down.

options.show: Sit down first, then jump up.
options.say: Sit down first, then jump up.

options.show: Jump up and sit down all at once.
options.say: Jump up and sit down all at once.

quiz.why: You must do the jumping action before you do the sitting action.

wrong.1: You must follow the order I said, which was jump first.
wrong.2: The instructions ask you to do them one after the other, not together.
wrong.3: You missed the first part of the instruction, which was to jump up.

quiz.say: What do you do when you hear, 'Take one big breath and then wiggle your fingers'?

options.show: Take a breath and wiggle your fingers at the same time.
options.say: Take a breath and wiggle your fingers at the same time.

options.show: Take a breath, then wiggle your fingers.
options.say: Take a breath, then wiggle your fingers.

quiz.why: This has two clear actions, so you must do them in the correct sequence.

wrong.0: The instructions say to do one thing, and then do the next thing.
wrong.1: You only did the first step and missed the second part of the instruction.
wrong.3: You forgot the first step, which was to take a big breath.
